Reference / db/sqlite

db/sqlite#

SQLite databases, in a file or in memory.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let db = await SqliteDatabase(path: Path("app.db"), options: SqliteOptions()).connection();
let scratch = await SqliteMemory().connection();
defer db.close();
await db.execution("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT)");
await db.execution("INSERT INTO notes(title) VALUES (?)", DbText("hello"));
let change = await db.transaction(options: TransactionOptions(), mode: SqliteTransactionMode.immediate);

Description#

SQLite databases, in a file or in memory.

By default a file is created when missing, foreign keys are on, there is no busy timeout and the journal mode is SQLite's own. A connection is also a DbConnection, so portable code and pools (through SqliteConnector or SqliteAcquiring) take it. The work runs on a native worker; calls never block the event loop. BLOB streaming, scripts and backups are in the submodules.

A refusal is a DbFailure with SQLite's extended result code ("SQLITE_1", "SQLITE_2067") and SQLite's own message ("no such table: notes"). Plain SQLITE_ERROR covers many failures, so its kind follows the message: a statement that does not compile is syntax, a limit is resource, an integer overflow is data, the rest unexpected.
